land.text: Starodub and the Severia towns that swore to the pretender in June 1607, with Orel as his winter base

predecessors.note: The pretender's lands were Tsardom of Russia land held by Tsar Vasily Shuisky; the Cliopatria shape of 1609-1611 drops the south-west band (320 k km2 between 30.6 and 46.3 E) which this dossier and the Polish lands account for.

land.text: the Kaluga lands of the pretender at his death: Kaluga, Tula, Bryansk, Orel, the towns round Moscow that swore to him in 1610

successors.note: After 11 December 1610 his Cossack camp at Kaluga stayed under his heir Ivan Dmitrievich ('Vorenok', ru page infobox) and its leaders joined the First and Second Militias; no page opened dates a successor state, so 1611 is left to the Tsardom (confidence 1). The Moscow government of the Seven Boyars (Semiboyarshchina) had expelled his governors from Serpukhov and Tula in late 1610.

capitals.name: Orel
capitals.note: Winter residence 1607-08: 'Лжедмитрий II перешёл в Орёл, ставший резиденцией самозванца во время зимы'. Coordinates are Orel city, approximate.

capitals.name: Tushino (Moscow)
capitals.note: Tushino Page: 'The Tushino camp was a replica of the Muscovite court, having its own prikazes and the Patriarch'; the ru page: in summer 1608 Tushino 'became his residence', 19 versts from the Kremlin. Coordinates approximate.

capitals.name: Kaluga
capitals.note: He fled to Kaluga on 27 December 1609 (6 January 1610), which 'became the pretender's new residence'; killed near Kaluga on 11 December 1610 and buried there. Coordinates approximate.

correction.text: Starodub, Karachev and Bryansk, the Severia towns that followed, and Orel, his winter residence of 1607-08

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria shape; Cliopatria's Tsardom of Russia keeps all of this to 1608). The ru page: on 12 (22) June 1607 'Стародуб присягнул на верность Лжедмитрию' and several southern cities followed; the en pages add 'Dmitry speedily captured Karachev, Bryansk, and other towns'. No boundary; admin-1 units are the reading.

correction.text: the Tushino lands of 1608: Tula, Kaluga, Orel, Severia, the centre (Yaroslavl, Kostroma, Vladimir, Vologda, Kashin), the east (Murom, Kasimov, Arzamas), Pskov in the north-west and the south with Astrakhan, round the Tushino camp near Moscow

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The ru page lists who 'swore' to the Tushino pretender (Pskov; Severia and the south with Astrakhan; Murom, Kasimov, Temnikov, Arzamas, Alatyr, Sviyazhsk; Suzdal, Uglich, Rostov, Yaroslavl, Kostroma, Vladimir; Tula, Kozelsk, Kaluga, Zvenigorod) and the en page 'the cities of Yaroslavl, Kostroma, Vologda, Kashin, and several others'. Oaths are not control: the map draws the sworn lands as the rebel's, hatched. Temnikov, Alatyr, Sviyazhsk, Zvenigorod and Kozelsk are not drawn separately (not in the gazetteer or inside a unit already named). No area is given on any page; the 1608 Tsardom shape (4.9 M km2) is not reduced by any ledger event of its own.

correction.text: the Tushino lands of 1608 less Galich, Vologda and Kostroma, which the popular movement of November 1608 turned against the pretender

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Time of Troubles page: 'In November 1608, a popular movement against the false Dmitrii started in Galich, and soon spread to Vologda and Kostroma'. The page does not say who held them afterwards; the Tushino camp stood until 'late December 1609' and sieged Moscow 'over the next eighteen months'.

correction.text: the Kaluga phase: his base at Kaluga, Tula and Severia (Bryansk, Orel), the towns that swore to him in 1610 (Kolomna, Kashira, Serpukhov, Borovsk, Suzdal, Galich, Vladimir) and the south-east

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the 545 central-Russian cells nobody holds in Cliopatria's 1610-1611. The ru page: 'Ему вновь присягнули многие города', 'Коломна, Кашира, Суздаль, Галич и Владимир', 'Его войска захватили Серпухов, Боровск', retook 'Козельск, Мещовск, Почеп и Стародуб' by September; the en Polish-Russian War page: he 'recovered a hold over all of south-eastern Russia' with the Don Cossacks. The Kazan and Vyatka oaths of 1610 are not drawn (distant, nominal). The pages do not name Orel, Tula or Tver for 1610: Orel and Bryansk follow from the Severia towns, Tula from the ru page's expulsion of his governors from Tula in late 1610; Tver is left out. Unverified: Ryazan, Lipetsk and the Don lands that 'south-eastern Russia' may include.

ledger.note: 22 June 1607 (12 June Old Style): Starodub swears to the Second False Dmitry. 'Стародуб присягнул на верность Лжедмитрию'; the en page has him first appearing 'around 20 July 1607, at Starodub' and, after 'In May 1607, accompanied by two aides, the impostor crossed the border', capturing 'Karachev, Bryansk, and other towns'. The two pages differ by a month; the ru date is used. The Bryansk oblast is the reading of the towns.

1607: 'several southern cities' follow Starodub (ru page) and 'Северщина и юг с Астраханью' stay under his rule. The Severia towns are named in the text; the Chernigov region (Chernigov and Severia) is the gazetteer's name for them.

December 1607: he winters at Orel. 'Лжедмитрий II перешёл в Орёл, ставший резиденцией самозванца во время зимы'; the move follows the December 1607 fighting at Bryansk. Rozhinsky beat Shuisky's army at Bolkhov on 30 April to 1 May (10-11 May) 1608.

region.text: Tula, which swore in the spring of 1608, and Kozelsk, Kaluga and Zvenigorod, whose gates opened

ledger.note: 1608: Tula and Kaluga go over to the pretender. 'Присягнула самозванцу также Тула, которая ещё совсем недавно целовала крест царю Василию'; 'Города Козельск, Калуга и Звенигород торжественно открыли свои ворота Лжедмитрию II'. The tsardom-of-russia ledger carries no matching loss.

region.text: Tushino, 'converted into an armed camp, where Dmitry gathered his army'

ledger.note: 1608: the pretender sets up his court at Tushino, 19 versts from the Kremlin. 'Advancing onward to Moscow, the second false Dmitrii set up court in Tushino, and laid siege to Moscow over the next eighteen months'; the Tushino page: 'settled in Tushino between 1608 and 1610'. The page gives no month; the ru page says summer 1608. The Tushino disc is a coordinate, not a gazetteer place.

region.text: Moscow and its environs besieged from Tushino

ledger.note: 1608: the siege of Moscow begins. Rozynski's men 'covered the areas west and south of Moscow, while Jan Piotr Sapieha's men covered the area north' (September 1608); Shuisky kept the city. The month of the first ground held is not on the page.

region.text: 'the cities of Yaroslavl, Kostroma, Vologda, Kashin and several others' and, in the centre, Suzdal, Uglich, Rostov, Yaroslavl, Kostroma, Vladimir

ledger.note: 1608: the northern and central towns swear to the Tushino court. He 'won the allegiance of the cities of Yaroslavl, Kostroma, Vologda, Kashin, and others' (Polish-Russian War page, Tushino camp 1608-1609); the ru page adds Suzdal, Uglich, Rostov and Vladimir. Allegiance, not occupation; admin-1 units are the reading of the towns.

region.text: in the east, Murom, Kasimov, Temnikov, Arzamas, Alatyr and Sviyazhsk

ledger.note: 1608: the Middle Volga towns recognise the pretender. 'На востоке власть тушинского «вора» признали Муром, Касимов, Темников, Арзамас, Алатырь, Свияжск'. Nizhny Novgorod and Kazan stayed with Shuisky (ru page).

region.text: in the north-west, Pskov and its suburbs

ledger.note: 1608: «На северо-западе самозванцу присягнули Псков и его пригороды». Novgorod stayed loyal to Shuisky.

region.text: 'Северщина и юг с Астраханью', Severia and the south with Astrakhan

ledger.note: The ru page says «Под властью Лжедмитрия II по-прежнему оставалась Северщина и юг с Астраханью» without a date for Astrakhan's oath; placed at the Tushino summit of 1608 as a bridge.

November 1608: the north turns on the pretender. 'In November 1608, a popular movement against the false Dmitrii started in Galich, and soon spread to Vologda and Kostroma.' The page does not say who held them afterwards; Tsar Shuisky's side is the reading. Galich is a coordinate disc, not a gazetteer place (the gazetteer's Galich is Halych in Ukraine).

Late December 1609: the Tushino siege ends. 'In late December 1609, the false Dmitrii fled for Kaluga. The "tsar's" departure caused the entire Tushino camp to break up in disarray.' The ru page gives 27 December 1609 (6 January 1610) and Tushino's end the next year under the Russo-Swedish army of Skopin-Shuisky and De la Gardie (Tushino page).

region.text: the Tushino camp and the northern, central, eastern and north-western towns that swore to it

ledger.note: 27 December 1609: the pretender flees Tushino for Kaluga and 'the entire Tushino camp' breaks up. The pages do not say who took each town: 'On 4 February 1610, the Russian lords formally in the Tushino court signed a treaty with Sigismund III' and Skopin-Shuisky with Swedish help drove out what remained (Tushino page), so the towns are read as returning to the Tsardom (or Sigismund's party). Bridging judgment; Astrakhan, Tula, Kaluga, Orel and Severia stay with the pretender in the 1610 keyframe.

region.text: Kolomna, Kashira, Suzdal, Galich, Vladimir, Serpukhov and Borovsk

ledger.note: Summer 1610: many towns swear to him again. «Лжедмитрию II присягнуло население многих городов и сел, в том числе ранее упорно боровшихся с ним: Коломна, Кашира, Суздаль, Галич и Владимир»; «Его войска захватили Серпухов, Боровск, Пафнутьев монастырь и дошли до самой Москвы». Kazan and Vyatka also swore (not drawn). The land belonged to the Moscow boyar government (Semiboyarshchina) during the Polish occupation.

region.text: Serpukhov and Tula, from which his governors were expelled

ledger.note: Late 1610 (no month on the page): the Semiboyarshchina «изгнало воевод самозванца из Серпухова и Тулы». In early December 1610 Zarutsky defeated Jan Sapieha's forces (ru page).

region.text: Kozelsk, Meshchovsk, Pochep and Starodub, retaken from the Poles

ledger.note: By early September 1610 the pretender's forces «отбили у поляков Козельск, Мещовск, Почеп и Стародуб». The page does not date their earlier loss to the Poles (Sigismund invaded in September 1609: Time of Troubles page); no loss is recorded for 1609-1610.

region.text: Kaluga, his base where he was killed, and the Severia lands

ledger.note: 11 December 1610: the pretender is killed. 'Dmitry was killed, while half drunk, on 11 December 1610 by a Tatar princeling, Peter Urusov'; the Polish-Russian War page has 20 December in another passage and the infobox 21 December (New Style). His Cossack camp and heir Ivan Dmitrievich are not drawn as a state; no page opened dates what held Kaluga in 1611.

wars.name: Second False Dmitry's rebellion and the siege of Moscow from Tushino
wars.outcome: The pretender took Severia, Tula, Kaluga and, from Tushino, besieged Moscow for eighteen months; the camp broke up in late December 1609 when he fled to Kaluga, and he was killed on 11 December 1610.
wars.note: Time of Troubles page. Before Sigismund's invasion (September 1609) the pretender was backed by Polish magnates ('supplying him with some early funds and about 7,500 soldiers', Polish-Russian War page).

wars.name: Polish-Russian War (1609-1618)
wars.outcome: Sigismund's September 1609 invasion made 'the majority of the Polish supporters of False Dmitry II desert him'; the pretender fled to Kostroma/Kaluga and was killed in 1610. The war's own zones belong to the Tsardom and Commonwealth dossiers.
wars.note: The Polish-Russian War page puts the flight to Kostroma first ('fled his camp disguised as a peasant and to go to Kostroma together with Marina') and later 'fled from Tushino ... to his base at Kaluga'; the Time of Troubles and ru pages date the Kaluga flight December 1609.

certainty.note: Every border here is a list of towns that swore allegiance; no page gives a line, and the ledger draws the sworn lands as admin-1 units or discs. Treat the Tushino extent of 1608 as the outer envelope of allegiance, not control.

sources.title: False Dmitry II
sources.note: Appearance at Starodub, 1608 advance, the allegiance of Yaroslavl, Kostroma, Vologda, Kashin, death on 11 December 1610. No Kaluga, Tula or Orel.

sources.title: Polish-Russian War (1609-1618)
sources.note: Tushino camp 1608-1609, Sigismund's intervention, desertions, flight to Kostroma and Kaluga, 'recovered a hold over all of south-eastern Russia', death 11/20 December 1610.

sources.title: Time of Troubles
sources.note: Tushino court, siege of Moscow, Rozynski and Sapieha, November 1608 Galich uprising, late December 1609 flight to Kaluga, 4 February 1610 treaty, death 11 December 1610.

sources.title: Tushino
sources.note: The Tushino camp as a replica of the Muscovite court, 1608-1610, flight to Kaluga in December 1609. Does not name towns.

sources.title: Лжедмитрий II (Russian Wikipedia)
sources.note: The only page opened that names the towns of the Tushino and Kaluga lands, the dates of Starodub (22 June 1607) and Kaluga (27 December 1609) and the 1610 oaths and losses. Read in Russian; quotes are the page's own words.

notes: Requested by the p1610-p1619 window (545 central-Russian cells nobody holds in Cliopatria's 1610-1611) and fed by the p1600-p1609 note. The English pages are thin on the pretender's extent: the en False Dmitry II page names only 'the cities of Yaroslavl, Kostroma, Vologda, Kashin, and several others' and 'a hold over all of south-eastern Russia', and none of the English pages opened names Tula, Orel or Kaluga in 1608-1610; the Russian Wikipedia article supplies the town lists and the 1607 and 1609-1610 dates and is the page the extent rests on. The lands are Tsardom of Russia land, so the tsardom-of-russia ledger needs the matching losses (1607 Severia, 1608 Tula, Kaluga, Tushino, the centre, the east, Pskov and Astrakhan; the 1610 oaths) and the gain back in 1609-1610; it carries none today, and its 1609 Cliopatria shape already lacks the south-west band, which this dossier and the Polish lands share. Not settled: the 1611 holder of Kaluga and Tula (the First Militia, Zarutsky's Cossacks and the heir Ivan Dmitrievich; no page opened); Marina Mniszech's status (the en pages give her at Tushino and Kostroma; the ru page does not tell her fate); Chernigov region as Severia (the Polish side held much of it after the 1609 invasion); whether the oaths of Pskov and Astrakhan meant control; who received the towns when the camp broke up. Gazetteer names needed: Tushino, Kashin, Galich (Kostroma Oblast; the gazetteer's Galich is Halych, Ukraine), Temnikov, Alatyr, Sviyazhsk, Kozelsk, Kolomna's neighbour Kashira. Type is rebel (a pretender's government with its own court and Patriarch); the Tushino camp also had a 'Patriarch' (Tushino page), name not on the pages opened. Wikidata id not known.
